chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Two men disputed before the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). One of them had purchased a camel from the other, and the seller had reserved the head and the skin. Then the buyer decided to sell it, so the Imam said to him: 'It is your partner in the camel, according to the measure of the head and the skin.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.اِخْتَصَمَ: disputed / brought a case to court

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of reserved parts in a partial animal sale according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the principle of partial ownership (*musha'*) in Islamic commercial law, where reserving specific parts of an animal creates a co-ownership structure rather than a complete retention of title. Imam Ali’s ruling clarifies that the buyer becomes a partner in the reserved portions proportional to their value, a nuance critical for resolving disputes in *bay'* (sales) contracts. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise contractual intent and the equitable distribution of rights in partial transactions.
